messages.author: 8ec8ec7ae5eef634
messages.subject: layout=daylight | Takes forever to run.
parts:
Hi, 

I am trying to visualize a tree with 944 leaves. This is how I am running it:

setwd("~/")
treefile <- system.file("~/", "Itf_Itb_Stb_Sch.phy.treefile", package="treeio")
iqtree_1 <- read.newick("~/Itf_Itb_Stb_Sch.phy.treefile")

#looking at tree
iqtree_1

#tree visualization
ggtree(iqtree_1, layout="daylight", branch.length = 'none')

It is running now for more than 2 hours. 

Is there something I can do better?

Thanks,

Camilo

messages.author: fa1e85b72b50d60b
messages.subject: Re: layout=daylight | Takes forever to run.
parts:
Hi, I've tested it with similarly sized datasets. It took about less than twenty minutes on my laptop.
Even if the computer hardware varies, I think the runtime for this amount of data should be within a predictable range.
You can try to see if on your computer my example can run in a certain amount of time.
If this example can be run through, I think you'll need to provide some information about the dataset in order to come to a conclusion about what to do next on this issue.
If this example can't be run in a certain amount of time, I think you need to think about your computer's hardware computing power and replace it with a machine with higher computing power. Of course, this is not an absolute, just FYI.

#a random tree
tree <- rtree(2020)
#tree visualization
ggtree(tree, layout="daylight", branch.length = 'none')
